title: Himanta Biswa Sarma Takes Oath as Assam CM for Second Term
excerpt: BJP-led NDA sweeps Assam with 102 of 126 seats, as PM Modi attends grand Guwahati swearing-in on May 12.
body:
Himanta Biswa Sarma was sworn in as Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term on May 12, 2026, at a packed ceremony at the Veterinary College Field in Khanapara, Guwahati — cementing BJP's dominance over India's northeastern gateway.

**What happened — a mandate and a moment:**
Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya formally appointed Sarma as Chief Minister on May 10 after he staked claim with the support of 102 MLAs in the 126-member Assembly. The BJP alone won 82 seats — crossing the outright majority mark for the first time in Assam's political history — with allies AGP and BPF adding 10 seats each. Sarma was unanimously elected leader of both the BJP Legislature Party and the NDA Legislature Party on May 9.

**Why it matters — Northeast power calculus:**
Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the ceremony as chief guest, joined by Home Minister Amit Shah and chief ministers from across NDA-ruled states — a rare show of national force for a state-level oath. The NDA's third consecutive Assam victory, with its biggest-ever seat tally, signals the party's tightening grip on the Northeast, a region that borders Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, and Myanmar. Sarma himself has emerged as the BJP's most influential operator in the region. He is now only the fourth person in Assam's history to serve as Chief Minister for a second consecutive term.

**What to watch — cabinet and governance priorities:**
Initial ministers sworn in alongside Sarma include Rameswar Teli, Atul Bora, Charan Boro, and Ajanta Neog, with a broader cabinet expansion expected in the weeks ahead as the new administration sets its legislative agenda.

nri_angle: For Indian-Americans with roots in Assam and the broader Northeast — a diaspora that spans communities in New York, New Jersey, and Texas — Sarma's second term will directly shape policies on land rights, infrastructure investment, and cross-border migration that affect families still living in the region.
